text:
anika: Quick heads-up — onboarding HydraCorp's adapter on our 13B checkout model revealed a nasty numeric/currency formatting regression during merge.
jorge: can you show a minimal before/after?
anika: baseline: `User: Show my invoice total\nAssistant: $3,210.75`\nmerged adapter: `User: Show my invoice total\nAssistant: 3 210 75` — dollar sign gone, decimals turned into spaces.
kai: that's pretty specific. does it affect other locales? GBP/JPY?
anika: spot-check: GBP baseline `£1,200.00` -> merged `1 200 00` ; JPY baseline `¥1200` -> merged `1200 ¥` (symbol moved to end).
samir: suggests learned template-like behavior from their training data. LoRA shouldn't touch tokenizer, but it can bias subtoken predictions. do you have decode traces?
anika: yes. token trace sample: ```baseline ids: [..., 210, 43, 7] -> [".", "75"] merged ids: [..., 210, 8932, 7] -> [" ", "75"]``` so a space-prefixed subtoken appears where punctuation previously was.
jorge: ugh. quantify impact with a quick eval pack and check quantized variants (int8/int4).
anika: running quick-eval (50 prompts covering USD/EUR/GBP/JPY, negatives, big numbers) now; writing CSV to s3://redwood-evals/hydra/quickpack-175999.csv. will share gist.
ops-bot: canary deploy for `hydra-adapter-merge` ran on eng-staging (4/4 checks) — rollout currently paused by manual flag.
kai: try merged + int4 quant locally; often quantization amplifies such tokenization biases.
anika: did that: int4 merged makes it worse (punctuation almost never predicted; symbols frequently appended to end).
samir: mitigation options: (1) short-term server-side postprocess: rejoin numeric tokens and re-insert currency symbol by locale, (2) request customer to retrain LoRA with explicit punctuation supervision and tokenization constraints, (3) attempt partial-merge (freeze some decoder layers) or low-epoch corrective fine-tune.
jorge: (1) fastest to unblock prod. infra: can we enable per-customer postprocess hooks?
kai: yes, we can add a per-route transform pipeline that runs a deterministic detokenize/normalize step. will prototype and measure latency.
anika: uploaded initial eval summary + token-diff: https://gists.example.com/hydra-175999-eval. summary: exact-match on numeric spans dropped ~29% merged vs baseline; int4 merged drop ~50%.
samir: that's too big to ignore. proposal: block production until mitigation applied or customer opts to retrain. add onboarding checklist item: numeric/currency formatting tests for all adapter merges.
jorge: agreed. i'll take point on customer comms and propose retrain or accept server-side mitigation.
kai: also will run a partial-merge experiment (freeze last 2 decoder layers) to see if issue localizes; if so, we can do a narrow revert instead of full rollback.
anika: opening onboarding ticket HYDRA-102 with artifacts, eval CSV, and recommended mitigations; assigning to @jorge for cust sync and @kai/@samir for infra/mitigation work. will update ticket with partial-merge results.
jorge: thanks. tag me when partial-merge data is in the ticket.
anika: will do. closing thread until we have the CSV + partial-merge numbers. :white_check_mark:
